perspective:
From Bradley Ochoa’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am Bradley Ochoa, a salesperson at a marketing firm. Katherine Lasiloo is my colleague and the marketing manager. We work together professionally; our relationship is generally cordial but can be strained when we disagree about sales versus marketing strategy.

- In a meeting room, I had prepared data and charts from our last five campaigns to support traditional sales methods. I told Katherine I appreciated her digital strategies but believed core sales could benefit more from traditional methods. She said the market is evolving, digital outreach has potential, and asked how I reconcile my data with increasing online engagement. I said I did not want to abandon digital marketing, but I was frustrated that proven traditional methods felt sidelined without proper consideration. She said she understood and suggested analyzing the data together to integrate both approaches.

- After that meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories that had boosted engagement and sales. I asked her to explain how those strategies are developed. She said it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk me through the analytics and decision-making behind a recent campaign. I admitted I had doubts about moving away from traditional methods, but seeing the outcomes made me want to understand the digital approach more. She said she was glad I was open to exploring it, that it is important to adapt to market trends, and that we should dive deeper into the data.

- I proposed a joint strategy meeting because I thought a combined approach could strengthen our campaigns. Katherine agreed and said we should schedule time to brainstorm and outline next steps. I said I was hopeful that leveraging both our expertise could create something impactful, and I thanked her for collaborating. She said she looked forward to it and that it was about leveraging each other’s strengths.

- After our joint meeting, I was excited and worked overtime to prepare a board presentation draft integrating both our ideas. I told Katherine about the draft and my excitement. She reviewed it, said it looked comprehensive and well thought out, and told me my hard work showed. I thanked her, said I was convinced the integrated approach would set us apart from competitors, and said I wanted to nail the presentation. She said she was confident we would, and suggested going through it once more to fine-tune areas if needed.

- After our presentation and the implementation of the new strategy, I felt grateful for my professional growth and our successful collaboration. I thanked Katherine, said I had learned a lot from her, and told her I was grateful for the growth I experienced through working together. She said it had been a pleasure seeing our project come to fruition and that my openness to new ideas made it a successful partnership. I proposed setting up regular strategy sessions to continue collaborating. She agreed, saying regular sessions would keep us on top of our game and market trends.

I do not have access to Katherine’s private thoughts, personality type, education, race, or any other information not directly stated to me or observed in these interactions.
